{{Top}}
{{Quote|What's the matter, Katarn? You've never heard of the turbolift? It's a lot easier than taking the stairs. It's faster too.|A [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] to [[Kyle Katarn]]|<ref name="RebelAgentAudio">[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent (audio drama)|''Dark Forces: Rebel Agent'' audio drama]]</ref>}}
[[File:Turbolift-KOTOR18.jpg|thumb|right|180px|A lift tube on the ''[[Arkanian Legacy]]'']]
A '''turbolift''', '''lift tube''', or simply '''lift''' was an "elevator" powered by a [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] and was used mostly to transport people or cargo through large ships, buildings such as those on upper [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], or even [[Space station/Legends|space stations]] such as [[The Wheel/Legends|the Wheel]] and the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Stars]].

They were capable of reaching great speeds without personal injury. The devices were sometimes referred to as '''turbovators''' rather than turbolifts; usage varied from world to world. [[Centerpoint Station]] referred to its elevator system that ran through [[Hollowtown]] and through the various metal shells as turbovators.

Though they provided a similar function, the [[drop shaft]] was distinctive from the turbolift.<ref name="Drop shaft">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse]]''</ref>

Some lifts would play [[lift-tube music]].

__TOC__

{{Noncanonstart|legends=1}}
==Known models==
*[[Infini-lift Lightspeed]]
*[[Insta-Lift 2000 SE]]
*[[NB200 Commercial Lift]]
*[[Ultra-Lift 3000 Extreme]]
{{Noncanonend}}

==Behind the scenes==
The obvious real-world equivalent would be an "elevator" (or "lift", in British English), with the difference that an elevator is moved by cables and machinery, while a turbolift is moved by a [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]]. "Turbolift" has often been shortened in various ''Star Wars'' media to "lift".
